chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Rayyan ibn Shubayb, who said:

Maradah bequeathed a bequest to a group of Christian workers. So our companions said, 'Distribute this among the poor believers from your companions.' So I asked Al-Rida (peace be upon him) and said, 'My sister bequeathed a bequest to a group of Christians, and I intended to divert that to a group of our Muslim companions.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Enforce the bequest upon what she bequeathed.'
Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: 'Indeed, its sin is upon those who alter it.'
ai.seo_question: Can a bequest to non-Muslims be redirected to Muslims according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Rida (peace be upon him) affirms the validity of bequests to non-Muslims, rejecting the narrator's desire to redirect funds to Muslims based on the principle of honoring the testator's explicit intent. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that a will is binding as written unless legally voided, emphasizing that the sin of alteration belongs to the one who changes it, rather than the bequest itself being invalid due to the recipient's faith. The citation of Quran 2:181 serves as the primary evidence, linking the prohibition of altering wills to the preservation of the deceased's wishes.
